messages.subject: Re: [seewave] sox alternative function sox_alt is now improved and modernized
messages.subject_clean: [seewave] sox alternative function sox_alt is now improved and modernized
messages.body_plain:
After discussing with Andre, this new version of sox() will be included in the next release of seewave.
Best
Jerome

De: "andremikulec" <andrem...@gmail.com>
À: "seewave GROUP" <see...@googlegroups.com>
Envoyé: Mercredi 29 Août 2018 22:11:18
Objet: [seewave] sox alternative function sox_alt is now improved and modernized

All,

The R CRAN package seewave function 'sox' does not work anymore (on Windows).

1. Inside the function "sox", the  hard coded windows path is no longer the latest version.
2. "sox" now has a widows installer. Spaces in the path2exe e.g. "Program Files"  causes an error.
3. On windows, an input of the path2exe  using backslashes(/) instead of slashes(\\) causes an error.
4. With the function sox, the examples of playing a wave file will no longer work, because the method has changed
(so the examples need to be fixed.)

For my own personal use, I rewrote sox as sox_alt
Here is the code (if anyone is interested.)

License is the same as  the R package seewave
License: GPL (>= 2)

The examples use a file that is attached.( "file590414e02032.wav" )
(The language is Spanish es-MX: words; Show the back translation window. )

Note: I added an extra "argus" arguments parameter.  This seems 'not immediately useful' but I did it anyways.
Also, the 'path and executable file' are now 'shell quoted.'

sox_alt <- function (command, exename = NULL, path2exe = NULL, argus = NULL, shQuote_type = NULL)
{

    if (is.null(exename)) {
      exename <- "sox"
    } else {
      exename = exename
    }

    if (is.null(path2exe)) {
      exe <- exename
    } else {
      path2exe <- normalizePath(path = path2exe, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
      exe <- paste(path2exe, exename, sep = "/")
    }

    if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {

        if(is.null(shQuote_type)) {
          shQuote_type = "cmd"
        } else {
          shQuote_type = "cmd2"
        }

    } else {  # .Platform$OS.type == "unix" # + Apple OS X + other

        if(is.null(shQuote_type)) {
          shQuote_type = "sh"
        } else {
          shQuote_type = "csh"
        }

     }

    exe <- shQuote(exe, type = shQuote_type)
    system(paste(exe, command, argus, sep = " "), ignore.stderr = TRUE)

}

# now does not assume to know the exact PATH ( because many versions exist including the latest )
# to play a .wav file sox/play now needs "-t waveaudio"
# write the path2exe using spaces
sox_alt(command = "file590414e02032.wav", path2exe = "C:\\Program Files (x86)\\sox-14-4-2" , argus = "-t waveaudio")

# write the path2exe using backslashes(/)
sox_alt(command = "file590414e02032.wav", path2exe = "C:/Program Files (x86)/sox-14-4-2"   , argus = "-t waveaudio")

# if sox, soxi, and play are in the %PATH%/$PATH . . .
# on Windows soxi.exe and play.exe are physical coplies of sox.exe
sox_alt(command = "file590414e02032.wav", argus = "-t waveaudio")
sox_alt(command = "file590414e02032.wav", exename = "play", argus = "-t waveaudio")
sox_alt(command = "file590414e02032.wav", argus = "-t waveaudio")

# get information
sox_alt(command = "file590414e02032.wav", exename = "soxi")
# Input File     : 'file590414e02032.wav'
# Channels       : 1
# Sample Rate    : 16000
# Precision      : 16-bit
# Duration       : 00:00:03.31 = 52960 samples ~ 248.25 CDDA sectors
# File Size      : 106k
# Bit Rate       : 256k
# Sample Encoding: 16-bit Signed Integer PCM

# old way still works
sox_alt("file590414e02032.wav slowfile590414e02032.wav tempo 0.5")

# old way: play a wave file or execute without using the "argus" parameter
sox_alt(command = "slowfile590414e02032.wav -t waveaudio")

--

> Dear all,
>
> It is my pleasure to announce the contest >spectro(2018), a friendly and informal contest for the best spectrogram generated with R code.
>
> The spectrogram is a 2D/3D key visualisation tool for bioacoustics, ecoacoustics and other sound related disciplines. The spectrogram is not only useful for science, it can also be a nice graphical object with delicate shapes and colours.

> . sound: .wav file / no limits, any recording (animal, habitat, voice, music, etc) or synthetic sound built with R
> . code: .r file / only within R language, any package but no call to external software, the code should be fully repeatable
> . image: static .png file / no limits in the choice of colour and size but should be readable on a web page

messages.subject: ffilter -- spectro
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,
dear Jerome Sueur,

I am using seewave meanwhile for a while. Now I am trying to use seewave for EEG analysis and it seems to works quite nicely. Nevertheless, I have two questions. Maybe someone can give me a short answer:

1. When doing "ffilter" on a time series with values between 10-30 (sampling rate f = 100) and filtering these times series for a band 8-12 Hz, I receive the filtered data. However, in what dimension are these new values?
The values now are much smaller than before and range between 1.99e-21 - 2e-19.

2. When doing "spectro" on the same data I get this nice time-frequency plot for which I can change the frequency range (flim). But how can I change the scale for the y-axis. Currently it is in kHz.
I would like to simply show Hz.

Thanks for answering

Lutz
